lyrics:
[Intro: banjo loop, a mower engine starts, low hum]

[Chorus: deep deadpan baritone, banjo and 808]
Yeah, I'm gonna ride my zero-turn
Down to the end of the cul-de-sac
Got a cupholder full of sweet iced tea
And I ain't never coming back
(Till lunch)

[Verse 1: half-rapped, trap hi-hats, banjo]
Got my cargo shorts and my grass-stain shoes
Sunscreen on my neck, I got nothing to lose
Neighborhood board says my edges ain't straight
Four miles an hour, they can wait

[Chorus: deep deadpan baritone, banjo and 808]
Yeah, I'm gonna ride my zero-turn
Down to the end of the cul-de-sac
Got a cupholder full of sweet iced tea
And I ain't never coming back
(Till lunch)

[Verse 2: gravelly older guest voice, played straight]
Mortgage paid off, son, that's my kind of flex
Grill so big it's got its own address
Kids think I'm corny, wife thinks I'm fine
Fella next door's got five horsepower, I got nine

[Bridge: beat drops out, banjo and whistle]
Ain't a soul alive can slow me down
(Honey! Lunch!)
Okay. Slowing down.

[Final Chorus: both voices, full beat]
Yeah, I'm gonna ride my zero-turn
Down to the end of the cul-de-sac
Got a cupholder full of sweet iced tea
And I ain't never coming back
(Till lunch)

[Outro: banjo loop, engine sputters and stops, spoken]
Out of gas.
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 68 BPM with double-time hi-hats, 4/4, G# minor. A slow, heavy swagger, completely serious about something small.

VOICE: Male baritone, deep, flat and deadpan, half-sung and half-rapped. Verse 2 is an older male guest with a gravelly, weathered voice who plays it straight. A woman's voice calls from a distance in the bridge.

INSTRUMENTS: A plucked banjo loop, booming 808 bass, crisp trap hi-hats and snare, a whistled answer line, a riding-mower engine at the start and end.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, banjo and engine. 0:08 Chorus 1. 0:30 Verse 1. 0:50 Chorus 2. 1:12 Verse 2, guest. 1:32 Bridge, beat out, the call to lunch. 1:44 Final chorus, both voices. 2:04 Outro, engine stops, two spoken words at 2:08.

PRODUCTION & MIX: 2019 country trap: dry banjo up front, huge clean sub bass, voice close and untreated apart from light doubling on the hook.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The small '(Till lunch)' after the first chorus at 0:27.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original is a young man's fantasy of freedom. This is what the fantasy looks like at fifty: the horse is a mower, the range is a cul-de-sac, and he is glad to be called home.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Swagger, more swagger, called in, content.
